protocol.py: 3 biology problems (1 error, 2 warnings).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 20 stocks
   line 36:  p20.aspirate(sample_volumes[i], source_plate[well_name])
   At line 36 the tip went into sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 2),
   sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2), sample 6 (well A6 in slot 2) and 16 more while it still
   carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in
   slot 2), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 39 more from an earlier step (this line did it
   20 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from
   them then took the unwanted material along into 20 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A6, A7,
   A8, A9, A10 and 12 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10 and 12 more in slot 2.
   Also reached 20 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10 and 12 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 36 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [3e1e31507258]

2. WARNING CONTAM-WELL: A used tip carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (well A2
in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 2), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 15 more into 3
wells it was never meant for
   line 37:  p20.dispense(sample_volumes[i], dest_plate[well_name])
   At line 37 the tip touched the liquid in wells A5, B1 and B10 in slot 3 while it still
   carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in
   slot 2), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 15 more from an earlier step (this line did it
   3 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into these wells on purpose, so it was
   not meant to be there. If the wells hold different samples, each now holds a little of
   another.
   Affected: wells A5, B1 and B10 in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 37. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense
   from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is
   already in the well.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   [e57386d7903b]

3. WARNING UNMIXED-AT-END: 19 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4
and 15 more went in (7 to 26% of the well)
   line 37:  p20.dispense(sample_volumes[i], dest_plate[well_name])
   At line 37 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 15 more to wells
   A1, A2, A3, A4, A6, A8, A9, A10 and 11 more in slot 3, which already held water (this
   line did it 19 times). The addition was 7 to 26% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a
   normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: 20 stocks
findings.explanation: At line 36 the tip went into sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 2), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2), sample 6 (well A6 in slot 2) and 16 more while it still carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 2), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 39 more from an earlier step (this line did it 20 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from them then took the unwanted material along into 20 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10 and 12 more in slot 3.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 36 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: A used tip carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 2), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 15 more into 3 wells it was never meant for
findings.explanation: At line 37 the tip touched the liquid in wells A5, B1 and B10 in slot 3 while it still carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 2), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 15 more from an earlier step (this line did it 3 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into these wells on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different samples, each now holds a little of another.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 37. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is already in the well.

findings.title: 19 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 15 more went in (7 to 26% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 37 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 15 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A6, A8, A9, A10 and 11 more in slot 3, which already held water (this line did it 19 times). The addition was 7 to 26% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A6, A8, A9, A10 and 11 more in slot 3 after line 37: `mix_after=(5, 40)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 40, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
